metadata.title: Learning remotely when schools close: How well are students and schools prepared? Insights from PISA (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The analysis draws on PISA 2018 microdata from representative samples of 15-year-olds across 79 education systems. The report presents descriptive indicators (e.g., access to a quiet place, computer, internet, and school-level preparedness measures) and does not provide a student-level modeling section where specific sampling or replicate weights would be named. In PISA, analysts typically use the complex survey design weights supplied in the PISA database to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors; however, this OECD note does not specify which weight variables (e.g., student sampling weights) were applied. Because the document is a descriptive policy note rather than a reproducible statistical model specification, the exact weighting and variance-estimation approach is not fully documented here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This OECD note reports descriptive percentages and cross-tabulated comparisons (e.g., by socio-economic school disadvantage/advantage) rather than estimating cognitive achievement outcomes using PISA plausible values. As a result, PV handling is not applicable to the reported indicators in this document. Missing-data handling is not described because the paper does not provide an analytic modeling workflow (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) for an ML or PV-based estimation task.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 data collected from representative samples of 15-year-olds across 79 education systems (as stated in the report). The note does not specify additional analytic restrictions (e.g., grade subsamples, item/module completion filters, or exclusions beyond the standard PISA sampling and questionnaire coverage for the reported indicators).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD policy note synthesizes evidence from PISA 2018 to assess how prepared students and schools are for remote learning during COVID-19 school closures. It reports descriptive indicators on students’ access to key home learning resources (quiet place to study, computer, and internet link) and on school preparedness (availability of computers and portability, teacher technical/pedagogical skills, time and professional resources for integrating digital devices, incentives/technical assistants, and whether an effective online learning support platform is available). The report highlights substantial within- and across-system inequalities, especially by socio-economic disadvantage at the school level, and emphasizes that technology access alone is insufficient without teacher capacity and guidance for students. It also notes a learning-relevant literacy finding from PISA 2018 (ability to distinguish fact from opinion) to argue that students may need structured teacher support to navigate online information. The document does not provide an ML modeling pipeline, PV estimation details, or explicit missing-data/weighting procedures for the reported percentages.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The document is a descriptive OECD policy note rather than an empirical ML study with a specified analytic sample size, per-country Ns, or a reproducible statistical modeling section. Consequently, fields such as total_students, per-country sample sizes, and ML/PV/missing-data handling are not reported in the text provided. The extraction therefore focuses on the stated PISA 2018 coverage (79 education systems; 600,000+ 15-year-olds) and the qualitative/percentage-based findings, without attempting to infer an ML estimation workflow.
